findings.claim: The landmark_00_local_dx coordinate proxy is non-monotone over the full observed window [0.0,0.49]: it rises to a positive peak near t≈0.11, falls to a negative trough near t≈0.19, partially recovers, and ends near its starting level. The whole-window mean z is small (-0.18), so the net endpoint change is weak relative to the within-window excursion.

The observed-node linear trend for landmark_00_local_dx has a strongly negative first rate (first_rate_z≈-17.5) and a strongly positive last rate (last_rate_z≈8.1), with 6 sign changes and 9 strong sign conflicts across 14 independent batches. This is a changing contrast, not a stationary target, and the polynomial fit was not accepted (polynomial_accepted=false, relative_node_RMSE≈0.78).

The score clock is observed at 50 nodes from 0.0 to 0.49 with learning window [0.0,0.5]; recorded affinities were removed and the label prior is equal. Selection preference is therefore association evidence only, not descendant survival or measured final benefit.

hypotheses.direction: no single monotone direction is supported; the observed contrast is positive early (peak near t≈0.11) and negative mid-window (trough near t≈0.19)
hypotheses.falsifier: a re-read of the same curve over the same support showing a monotone profile, or a whole-window mean z inconsistent with the reported near-zero net change
hypotheses.observable: landmark_00_local_dx (predicted endpoint world A feature, z-scored)
hypotheses.scope: global over the observed score-node window [0.0,0.49]; no extrapolation beyond 0.49
hypotheses.statement: If the landmark_00_local_dx coordinate proxy is controlled, the supported observable is its signed z-scored value over the observed score-node window [0.0,0.49]; the observed profile is a rise-then-fall contrast with a positive excursion near t≈0.11 and a negative excursion near t≈0.19, so any reward should be evaluated against this non-monotone shape rather than a single endpoint target.

hypotheses.direction: early negative rate, late positive rate; no absolute coordinate target is specified by these rates
hypotheses.falsifier: a re-read showing first_rate_z and last_rate_z of the same sign, or fewer than the reported sign changes
hypotheses.scope: observed score nodes only; the derivative contrast does not define an absolute coordinate target or spatial gradient
hypotheses.statement: If a temporal dose recipe is applied to this coordinate, the first-rate and last-rate signs (negative early, positive late) imply the controlled contrast changes sign within the window; a recipe that assumes a stationary target or a single endpoint direction would be mismatched to the observed 6 sign changes and 9 strong sign conflicts.

limitations: Only one coordinate feature (landmark_00_local_dx) was read; other landmark coordinates and soft_mass features were not queried, so cross-feature consistency is unverified.
Stage profiles and temporal profiles are unavailable; no stage boundary or phase knot is supported by data.
The polynomial fit was not accepted and relative_node_RMSE is high, so the quadratic coefficients should not be treated as a validated trajectory model.

Selection preference is association evidence only; no descendant survival, last recorded joint-head score, or decoded final affinity was observed, and missing decoded labels are unobserved rather than failures.
No energy or chemical-interaction interpretation is attached to this untyped coordinate proxy.
